parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish اویماق, ultimately from Classical Mongolian ᠠᠶᠢᠮᠠᠭ (ayimaɣ, “tribe”). Compare Mongolian аймаг (ajmag), Buryat аймаг (ajmag), Kalmyk әәмг (äämg); and in Turkic languages, Yakut аймах (aymax), Kyrgyz аймак (aymak), Kazakh аймақ (aymaq), Uyghur ئايماق (aymaq).

parole.significato: Thin rope or twine typically made from flax or hemp fibers
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish سجیم (sicim, “string, cord, twine”) (alternative forms; سجم, سیجیم), possibly from Classical Mongolian ᠰᠢᠴᠢᠮ (sičim, “rope”) but this is not certain. Cognates with Azerbaijani sicim, Karachay-Balkar джиджим (cicim), Karakalpak şıjım, Nogai şıjım.
